end.summary:
Practised dot pictures for triangular and square-number sequences.
Explained that a new square grows by adding one row and one column, with the corner counted once.
Used the L-shape to explain the odd-number jump: 2n + 1.
Initially mixed up the square total with the number of added dots; later corrected this distinction.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised showing sequence growth with dot pictures and used the shared-corner idea to explain why the added L-shape has 2n + 1 dots. They also connected this to the fact that 2n + 1 is odd. There was a mix-up between the total dots in a square and the dots added to make the next square, and it was corrected later in the lesson (correctAfterLastSeen: true). At home, ask them to draw 4×4 and 5×5 squares and label both the total dots and the added L-shape.
